differences.what: massing: a broad brick block two tall storeys over a raised basement, its north flank receding to the rear, a swell bay at the north end of the front and a wing at the south end; the draft stood a 11.5 m hipped box with no bay, wing or flank windows
differences.how: T-2441: K01 frontage on the 1911 sheet's plan at the trace's own 13.1 m width and 11.0 m depth; the four plan corners land on the engraving's (x 92, 255, 617 and 800 px) exactly, by the camera's solve

differences.what: storey lines: the principal floor about 2.3 m over grade, the second floor about 6.6 m, the cornice's soffit about 11.5 m; the principal windows 3.0-5.7/6.0 m, the second storey's 7.2-9.5 m
differences.how: T-2441: a 2.3 m principal floor and 4.3 and 4.9 m storeys; the cornice and the second storey's sills and heads fall within about 15 px of the engraving's on the camera's own 4-13 px height residual

differences.what: the swell bay: from grade nearly to the cornice, about 4.8 m on its chord from the north corner to the door, three windows a storey round it
differences.how: T-2441: a K08 bow, 4.8 m chord and 1.3 m rise at s 2.72 m, two storeys of three sashes at -36, 2 and 40 degrees, to 10.7 m; the three windows' columns land at x 320, 400 and 458 px against the engraving's 325, 412 and 458

differences.what: the entrance between the bay and the wing, up a stoop, under one window of the second storey and a dormer
differences.how: T-2441: the K07 door on the middle front bay at 6.25 m (x 515 px), its window over it and the dormer over that

differences.what: the stacks: two tall stacks on the north wall near its front and its rear, one over the wing
differences.how: T-2441: three K01 stacks at the engraving's columns (x 225, 135 and 690 px) and at the tops it reads (16.4, 15.5 and 14.8 m). The third is the Grosvenor photograph's stack on the south wall (T-2781): the two pictures' rays through it meet at u 6.47, v 13.37, so it stands on the south wall's cornice at u 6.5, v 13.2, 1.2 by 0.75 m, and not over the wing at u 10.2, v 11.2, where T-2465 had stood it on this camera's ray alone. Through this camera its shaft stands at x 660-710 px against the drawn 663-717 (the cap's spread to 654-716) and its top at 15.85 m at about y 114 against 113, behind the wing's hipped crown. T-2782: those tops are now the pots' lips, the caps 0.56 m under them (the crowns' item)

differences.what: the wing: the engraving draws it standing well forward of the front and rising under its own steep hipped roof, as high as the main roof, with a stack at its ridge; the build stands it on the 1911 sheet's 1.0 m step under the mansard's cornice, with a flat tin deck
differences.how: T-2465: the wing hipped to its own ridge by K01's mansard crown built as a hip (mansard.crown.form: hip), its fascia's top on the main eave and its cornice 0.55 m past the wing's face: the sides and back at 45.5 degrees, so the ridge stands at 14.5 m (its apex at y 137 px against the drawn 142), 0.4 m over the main curb, and runs 1.9 m back into the main roof; the street end at 60 degrees, so it stands whole in front of the main lower faces up to the curb, as drawn. The engraving's apex stands about 45 px left of the build's (x 640 against 685): no symmetric hip on the 1911 sheet's 1.0 m step stands its apex that far back and still clears the main lower faces, which is the draughtsman's perspective (the camera's solve). The wing still stands on the sheet's 1.0 m step, which controls the plan. The stack the engraving draws at the wing's ridge stands behind it on the south wall (T-2781, the stacks item)

differences.what: the main roof: steep straight lower faces in slate under a level top line, hipped down at the wing; the build's K05 mansard has convex lower faces 2.6 m tall
differences.how: T-2452: K05's mansard laid with no bulge, so each lower face is one straight plane from the cornice to the curb at 14.1 m, the engraving's level top line, and the upper hip at 10 degrees stays behind that line from the camera. The faces stand at 65 degrees, the floor of K05's range; the engraving's hip ends lean back further than that, by a perspective that is not one camera's (L-k01-1637-spalding-remodel-2441)

differences.what: the dormers: two gabled dormers with square-headed sashes on the street face and one on the north face; the build's are K01's round-headed mansard dormers at the same places
differences.how: T-2452: K01's gabled lower-face dormer: a square-headed two-over-two sash 0.9 by 1.2 m in a stone face 1.6 m wide under a 40 degree pediment, slated cheeks and slopes, on T-2441's centres over the bay and the door. The street pair's faces span about x 349-417 and 492-555 px against the engraving's about 323-413 and 469-553 with their rakes, each about 15 px right of the engraving's as the door under it is; their apexes about 10 px under the engraving's. The pediment's slight rake overhang is not built

differences.what: the windows: the principal storey's about 2.9 m tall, the wing's a French window to its floor over a balcony; the build's are 2.4 m sashes, the K01 contract's clear-height limit
differences.how: T-2534: the principal storey's sashes 2.95 m over their 0.7 m sill on the house and 3.0 m over grade on the bay, on the engraving as their source and past K01's 2.4 m starting height, so their heads stand at 5.95 m: through the camera the bay's span y 507-637 px against the engraving's 502-632. The wing's is K06's French pair under a four-light transom, 1.9 m wide and 3.35 m tall on a threshold 0.05 m over the balcony's floor: x 672-742 px and its head at y 520 px against the engraving's 672-745 and 518

differences.what: the wing's second-storey window: one opening about 1.8 m wide (x 675-745 px), a pale bar down its middle (x 704-707 px) and in each half a meeting rail and no bars, two one-over-one sashes; the build had a single 1.1 m sash (x 688-730 px)
differences.how: T-2537: K06's paired flat-headed sash, 1.8 m clear, two 0.88 m lights on a 0.04 m mullion (the mullion's width reconstructed, L-k01-1637-wing-pair-2537), at the 2.1 m height and 0.75 m sill it had; through the camera it spans x 675-743 px, its mullion at x 709-710, and its lights y 353-445 px as the print's

differences.what: the stoop's landing railed, its rail about 1.0 m over the landing (y 623-675 px)
differences.how: T-2447: K07's turned balustrade on both cheeks, level beside the landing and raked down the flight, 1.0 m over the landing

differences.what: the stoop's flight: the engraving draws its foot at the fence's first post (x 557 px), well short of the walk; K07's straight flight reaches about 1.6 m past the garden's line, so the built fence starts at about x 640 px
differences.how: T-2535: the stoop shortened to the drawn foot: K07's fourteen whole risers on the K01 contract's shortest going (0.25 m) and a 1.1 m landing, so the flight reaches 4.35 m before the front (5.1 m before), and its north cheek's foot lands at x 560 px against the drawn 557. The fence still starts at the stoop's south cheek on the garden line (x 642 px): through the camera the drawn post stands in front of the flight's foot, and a fence across a flight is what the K11 kit refuses, so the post is read as the foot's place (L-k01-1637-basement-lights-2535). The engraving draws the cheek's rail level to the post where the build's rakes down the flight: at this camera's distance a level rail and a raked one differ by about 90 px, so the drawn stoop's rise is the draughtsman's, and the stair stays K07's

differences.what: the wing's balcony on its principal floor, bowed, about 0.9 m high under the French window
differences.how: T-2534: K08's floor balcony on the wing's front at the principal floor (2.3 m): a stone slab 0.2 m deep on a bow 3.4 m on its chord, and on it a stone balustrade 0.9 m high, square balusters at 0.17 m under a coping, which the engraving draws pale as it draws the stoop's stone rail: x 649-772 px and its coping at y 627 px against the engraving's 651-779 and 630. Its rise, 0.6 m, the engraving's nearly frontal view does not give (L-k01-1637-wing-balcony-2534)

differences.what: the wing's second-storey window: the engraving draws it as wide as the French window under it, about 1.8 m (x 675-742 px), divided by a mullion; the build's is a 1.1 m sash (x 686-728 px)
differences.how: T-2537: the same window as the item above, filed twice; T-2537 built it (K06's paired sash, x 675-743 px) and this copy was left open (T-2755)

differences.what: the basement's lights: two round-headed under the wing, one nearly a storey tall under the bay
differences.how: T-2535: under the bow one barred, flat-headed light 1.0 m wide and 1.3 m tall over a 0.5 m sill, carried by the bay under its middle window: x 382-419 px and y 696-752 px against the drawn 388-439 and 696-757 (the bow's windows stand about 12 px left of the engraving's throughout, as built since T-2441); under the wing a pair of round-headed lights, each a two-light sash under a fanlight (K06's sash_round_fanlight_wide at a basement light's size, the engraving's upright and cross bar), 0.9 m wide and 1.4 m to the crown over a 0.3 m sill, 0.7 m apart, centred under the French window: x 665-697 and 728-760 px against the drawn 675-710 and 736-771, their crowns at y 695 px against 692

differences.what: the wing rises to the cornice itself in the engraving, its cornice level with the main one's; the build stopped it at 10.7 m, under K10's bed moulding
differences.how: T-2465: the wing's walls carried to 11.35 m, into the soffit of its hipped crown (11.3 m), the crown's cornice level with the main one's; K10's bed moulding runs into its cheeks and its brackets stop short of it

differences.what: the swell bay rises to the cornice itself in the engraving; the build stops it at 10.7 m, under K10's bed moulding
differences.how: T-2472 carried the bow's upper storey to the foot of K10's bed moulding and swept the cornice round its plan; T-2782 withdrew that on the item below, the engraving read again: the bow does not rise into the cornice but stops under a dark cap of its own (y about 255-270 px on its crown) with the main cornice running straight over it. Built so: its wall top at 10.95 m under K08's own soffit and 0.2 m fascia, clear of the bed moulding, its cap at y 262-276 px on its crown

differences.what: over the swell bay the engraving draws the main cornice running on straight, a band above the bow's own cap (y about 207-255 px), where the build's eave, about 0.3 m under the engraving's cornice line all along the front (its soffit at 11.3 m since T-2528, 11.21 m before it, against the engraving's about 11.5 m), is the bow's cap itself and is carried round it
differences.how: T-2782: the bow stopped under the main cornice with a cap of its own (the item above), so the house's bed moulding, soffit, fascia and gutter run on straight along the front over it, unbroken, as drawn: through the camera the main cornice's fascia and gutter at y 250-258 px over the bow's cap at 262-276. The band's height is argued, not built. The engraving's cornice line is not one line through this camera: its dark band reads y 207-215 px north of the left dormer and y 228-240 over the door, 20 px apart along 2 m of straight wall, more than the solve's 4-13 px height residual. And it cannot be met without breaking two matched items: the wall head raised 0.3 m (tried, T-2782) either takes the mansard's level top line from 14.1 m to 14.4 m, past the engraving's (T-2452), or, with the lower faces shortened to keep it, leaves the street dormers' heads (2.43 m over the eave) above the curb; and the wing's hipped crown, slated over 45 degrees, rises with it to at least 14.75 m, its apex about 16 px over the drawn one where it now stands 5 px over (T-2465). So the eave stays on T-2441's storey lines, the soffit at 11.3 m (T-2528)

differences.what: the stacks' panelled shafts and caps
differences.how: T-2471: the K15 kit's carved head on the three stacks (k15.stack.sherman less its stone bands and corbel blocks): three corbelled brick courses under a 0.14 m stone cap projecting 0.15 m, the head's step out reading at each stack's top as the engraving's does; on the two tall north stacks and the south one (T-2781) a sunk panel 0.45 m wide on the street face (and the rear), from 0.5 m over the roof to 0.3 m under the head, where the engraving draws the tall front stack's lit face as a long light field in a dark border. T-2782: with its cap lowered under its pots the rear north stack has 0.41 m of shaft for a panel, and the engraving draws that stack's face hatched through with no light field, so it is plain; the front stack's panel is 1.31 m, the south's 0.98 m

differences.what: a dark hooded crown over each stack's cap, about 0.4-0.5 m tall
differences.how: T-2782: a clay pot of the K15 kit's plain profile (0.56 m) on each stack's two flues, and each cap lowered 0.56 m, so the pots' lips stand at the tops read before. The crowns read 20-27 px tall on the plate, 0.5-0.6 m: through the camera the pots' lips land at y 29, 108 and 111 px against the drawn 24, 104 and 113, the caps at y 50-55, 127 and 131-137 against the drawn shoulders' 51-53, 128 and 133-137, the two pots spanning about the crown's width. The hood's turn over one side is a cowl's, or a pot's under a hood, which the plate's scale does not settle (L-k01-1637-stack-pots-2782)

differences.what: the wing's cornice: the engraving draws it as a band as deep as the main cornice's (y 232-262 px), with a block in it over the window; the build's is the crown's K05 fascia, 0.2 m deep, without K10's brackets
differences.how: T-2467: K10's bracketed timber cornice, the house's own, carried round the wing's three faces under its crown's soffit on the main wall head's line (wall_head.crown), so the band, the crown's fascia over the brackets, spans y 258-265 px at its top to 293-299 at the brackets' feet, 35 px as the main cornice's 258-293, where the fascia alone was 9 px; and a timber block on the window's centre, 0.75 m wide, from the brackets' feet through the fascia to 0.15 m over it, at x 709-738 px against the engraving's about 700-730, rising about 6 px over the band as the engraving's does. The band stands about 30 px under the engraving's with the whole eave (the open storey-line item above), and the brackets are K10's where the engraving draws a plain band, as on the main front

differences.what: the brick garden wall before the north flank, ending in a square pier before the swell bay (x 357 px), and the iron spear fence before the wing, both close before the house, the fence's top rail about 1.9 m over grade
differences.how: T-2447: K11's front-garden layout on one line 3.5 m before the main front (the runs' feet, y 777-787 px, read on the camera's ground there): the kit's brick wall, 2.0 m with 2.25 m piers, its end pier at x 357 px as drawn; the kit's spear fence from the stoop's south cheek to the lot line, its top rail 1.9 m over grade

differences.what: the garden wall runs on north past the frame's edge, about 3.5 m beyond the 1911 lot line through this camera, onto the unbuilt strip prairie_1625_1637_c
differences.how: not 1637's, and not this picture's to say for 1904 (T-2782): the run past 1637's lot line (s -3.14 to about -6.6 m on the wall's line, u 14.5) falls inside the Forsyth house's footprint at 1635 (forsyth_house_1635_prairie, Robinson 1886's outline, standing 1863 to after 1902), whose south wall stands on the 1911 lot line and whose front stands 3.1 m before the wall's line, at u 17.6. The engraving omits that house altogether: on this camera it would stand between the eye and the lower north flank, which the engraving draws whole, so the draughtsman cleared the neighbour, and the wall's run on north is drawn across ground the house stood on. 1637's wall rightly stops at its own line (T-2443, #771)

differences.what: colour: the engraving is monochrome
differences.how: the brick and trim colours stay reconstructed

differences.what: the south wall, the rear and the rear range
differences.how: built on the 1911 sheet at the reconstructed tier (L-k01-1637-spalding-remodel-2441)

differences.what: the walk: the engraving draws a light walk at the stoop's foot, between the garden wall's end pier and the fence's first post, curving out toward the street; the build had none
differences.how: T-3221: a flagged walk laid from the stoop's foot, its 1.8 m width, out through the gap between the wall and the fence (s 0.87 to 7.55) to the public walk. It runs straight where the engraving curves it, a difference in the walk's line inside the garden's gap of well under a foot at the stoop and a few feet at the street: within tolerance for a reconstructed walk (L-k14-walks-1600-block-3215)

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
